title: Dynamic slot pacing and cold-KV reclamation for disparate prompt/response distributions
text:
Dynamic slot pacing and cold-KV reclamation for disparate prompt/response distributions

description:
Background: Production traffic exhibits a bi-modal distribution: short prompts with long continuation (chatty assistants) and long single-shot prompts with short responses (batching inference). The current continuous batching scheduler packs by arrival time and a coarse length bucket which causes two problems: 1) KV cache fragmentation and growth from many long-lived response KV entries, and 2) GPU memory slab fragmentation that increases tail latency during peak mixes.

goal:
Reduce p99 latency by at least 15% for mixed-length traffic at target throughput while keeping token cost within 5% of baseline and reducing average KV memory footprint per GPU by 20%. Enable a safe rollout path with feature flagging and canarying.

success_metrics:
p50 latency (tokens): maintain or improve
p95 latency (ms): reduce by >= 10%
p99 latency (ms): reduce by >= 15%
GPU memory headroom: increase free slab by >= 20%
KV cache occupancy: reduce mean bytes/GPU by >= 20%
token-cost delta: within +5% of baseline

design_summary:
Introduce two coordinated runtime mechanisms: 1) Dynamic slot pacing: the scheduler measures in-flight slot occupancy and applies short-pulse pacing to defer low-priority long-response allocations during high short-prompt bursts. Pacing uses a soft budget token per-slot that replenishes over time, preventing starvation. 2) Cold-KV reclamation + soft-TTL: mark KV banks as cold if not referenced in the last N steps and evict lazily during low utilization windows. Combine with per-shard compact-on-evict to return GPU slab memory to the allocator to reduce fragmentation. The scheduler considers per-request 'continuation-likelihood' heuristic (past-turn length, model type) to decide prefetch vs reserve behaviors.

tradeoffs_and_considerations:
- Aggressive KV eviction reduces memory but can increase recompute if evicted entries are reused. To mitigate, we threshold eviction based on recent reuse rate and provide a small MRU cache region.
- Pacing introduces small added latency for some long-response requests; we cap max defer to 40ms default and expose policy knobs.
- Compact-on-evict has overhead; we schedule compaction during predicted low-utilization windows (observed from historical traffic patterns).
- Heuristics may require per-customer tuning for Dedicated deployments; plan to provide conservative defaults and expose knobs in Console.

implementation_steps:
1) Add in-flight slot accounting and per-slot soft budget tokens (runtime change)
2) Implement short-pulse pacing policy with default parameters and feature flag (FF_BATCH_PACING)
3) Add KV coldness tracker + soft-TTL and lazy-evict path (FF_COLD_KV)
4) Implement per-shard compact-on-evict and async compaction scheduler
5) Add metric instrumentation: kv_evictions, kv_reclaims_bytes, slot_defer_count, slot_replenish_rate
6) End-to-end unit tests and stress harness for mixed-length workloads
7) Create canary plan and rollout automation (console feature flag + telemetry alerts)
8) Run multi-customer A/B canary for 2 weeks, evaluate metrics, iterate

testing_plan:
We will run three testbeds: 1) synthetic bi-modal traffic generator (short prompts, long replies), 2) replay of sampled production traces from last 30 days, 3) limited live canary (5% traffic). For each: measure latency distribution, KV occupancy, slab fragmentation via existing heap histograms, and end-to-end token cost. Add deterministic unit tests for KV coldness state transitions and compaction triggers.

baseline_metrics:
(sampled from 2026-02-01 production cluster)

baseline_values:
median latency: 45 ms
p95 latency: 160 ms
p99 latency: 420 ms
avg GPU free slab: 2.1 GB
kv occupancy per-GPU: 28 GB
token-cost: $0.0039 per 1k tokens

experimental_results:
experiment A (local cluster, 8-GPU nodes, mixed 60/40 short/long): p99 reduced from 420ms to 340ms (19% improvement), kv occupancy down 22%, GPU free slab up to 2.7GB
experiment B (trace replay): token-cost +1.8%, p95 -12%
notes: heavy reuse patterns saw lower eviction rates; tuned soft-TTL from 15s -> 45s for those tenants

rollout_plan:
Feature-flagged rollout: enable FF_BATCH_PACING and FF_COLD_KV behind runtime flags. Stage 1: internal staging for 48h. Stage 2: canary 5% of hosted API traffic for 72h with automatic rollback triggers: kv_evicts_rate > 3x baseline or p99 latency regress > 10%. Stage 3: ramp to 25% for 7d, then 100% after validation. For Dedicated customers, provide opt-in and a conservative default policy.

monitoring_and_alerting:
Dashboards: 'batching/slot-pacing' and 'kv/reclaims' panels. Alerts: p99 latency increase > 10% (5m window), kv_evictions spike > 2x baseline (1m window), GPU free slab drop > 30% (10m). Add tracing tags: slot_paced=true, kv_evicted=true for root-cause analysis.

acceptance_criteria:
Canary run meets success_metrics for at least 95% of windows
No customer-facing errors introduced (5xx rate within baseline)
Controlled token-cost increase <= +5%
Runtime and unit tests passing in CI
Runbook updated with rollback steps and tuning knobs

comments:
2026-02-12 Priya Shah: Initial triage — confirmed gap in KV growth during mixed traffic. Proposed soft-TTL approach in design doc.
2026-02-20 Evan Martinez: Added slot-token prototype. Local microbench shows reduced preemption in short-prompt bursts.
2026-02-25 Mei Chen: Implemented coldness tracker; seeing errant evictions in synthetic workloads when TTL < 10s. Increasing default to 30s.
2026-03-02 Sofia Lopez: Dashboards updated in staging with kv_evictions and slot_defer_count. Noted correlation between slot_defer spikes and p95 improvements.
2026-03-10 Liam O'Connor: Canary targets defined; communicated to SRE and customer success for monitoring.
2026-03-12 Evan Martinez: Mid-canary update: p99 has dropped ~17% on canary nodes; one tenant shows higher recompute — rolling back for that tenant and adjusting soft-TTL to 60s for their profile.

runbook_and_rollback:
Runbook stored in Confluence link above. Rollback steps: 1) turn off FF_BATCH_PACING and FF_COLD_KV via feature flags; 2) trigger immediate KV reclaim pause and revert compaction scheduling; 3) notify customers on canary and open incident if p99 regressions persist. Post-rollback: gather traces and iterate on heuristics.

notes:
This work aims to be conservative for Dedicated customers by default. We will add an admin knob in Console 'kv_eviction_aggressiveness' with three tiers (conservative, balanced, aggressive) and surface expected memory vs recompute trade-offs. Consider follow-up: persistent KV advisory that predicts eviction cost for private deployments.
